question: I have a gene expression matrix in CSV format. Generate a clustered heatmap using row-wise Z-score normalization and default hierarchical clustering. Label samples and genes clearly.

files.eval_guideline: Heatmap must show row Z-score coloring with hierarchical clustering dendrograms on both axes and labeled genes and samples; color palette and font size may differ.
files.match_reasoning: Both files have the identical filename clustered_heatmap.png and PNG image format, directly corresponding to the requested clustered gene expression heatmap. The matching task identifier b-3-1 further supports this correspondence.
files.strategy_reasoning: The guideline requires visual confirmation of row-wise Z-score coloring, hierarchical clustering dendrograms on both axes, and clear gene and sample labels. Semantic comparison accommodates the explicitly permitted differences in color palette and font size.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images show the same apparent 100-gene by 20-sample expression matrix with row-wise Z-score coloring, hierarchical clustering dendrograms on both axes, and gene and sample labels. Sample ordering matches, including the major division between Samples 1–10 and Samples 11–20. Gene ordering and distinctive cell patterns also match, such as the strongly negative Gene_80/Sample_6 cell and strongly positive Gene_51/Sample_16 cell. Both convey the same dominant pattern of relatively lower expression in the left sample cluster and higher expression in the right cluster. Their color bars identify row Z-scores with comparable ticks from −2 to +2. The candidate uses a more saturated diverging palette, omits visible white cell borders, and provides more readable gene labels through its taller layout. Its title additionally specifies average linkage and Euclidean distance, although the title sits close to the upper dendrogram. These presentation differences do not alter the scientific content or interpretation; no critical elements are missing.
